# Lifecycle — service start-up and soft dependencies (server)

**Core** (always installed).

## `GaxiaServer.Lifecycle`

- Runs: **server only (Script / server ModuleScript)**
- Source: `src/ServerStorage/Gaxia_Packages_Server/Lib/ServiceLifecycle.lua`

Get it:

```lua
local GaxiaServer = require(game:GetService("ServerStorage").Gaxia_Packages_Server)
local Lifecycle = GaxiaServer.Lifecycle
```

### Functions

- `Lifecycle.Define(module: {}, spec: Spec): ()`
  Register a service's lifecycle. Call it as the module's LAST statement (after every function is defined) — it is pure metadata and starts nothing.
- `Lifecycle.Ensure(module: {}): boolean`
  Start `module` (and its Needs) now if it has a spec and has not started yet. Returns true when the module is initialised (or has no spec).
- `Lifecycle.EnsureAuto(module: {}): boolean`
  The loader's start-on-access: like Ensure, but respects AutoStart = false.
- `Lifecycle.Boot(modules: { {} }): ()`
  Start every module in `modules` (Features order, Needs first): all Inits, then all Starts.
- `Lifecycle.GetState(module: {}): State?`
- `Lifecycle.GetStateByName(name: string): State?`
- `Lifecycle.GetStarted(): { string }`
  Names of initialised services, in the order they started.
- `Lifecycle.IsBooted(): boolean`
- `Lifecycle.OnBooted(fn: () -> ()): ()`
- `Lifecycle.OnInitialized(module: {}, fn: () -> ()): ()`
  Run `fn` once `module` is initialised (now, on a new thread, if it already is), however it gets started — for soft dependencies ("use it if it runs").
- `Lifecycle.OnAnyInitialized(fn: (name: string) -> ()): ()`
  Run `fn(name)` every time any service finishes Init (used by the loader to publish the started set to clients).
- `Lifecycle.SetResolver(fn: (name: string) -> {}?): ()`
- `Lifecycle.Find(name: Types.ServiceName): any`
  Soft dependency: the service registered as `name`, or nil when its package is not installed. Loads the module if it is installed but not loaded yet; never starts it (calling one of its functions does, unless it is AutoStart = false). Call it from Start / functions (it may load the server loader, which can yield), never from a module body or an Init, and cast the result to the few members you use: type PetApi = { GetCoinMultiplier: (player: Player) -> number } local Pet: PetApi? = Lifecycle.Find("Pet")
- `Lifecycle.Register(service: Service): ()`
  Queue a service. Registration ORDER is the dependency order (register a service after the ones it depends on).
- `Lifecycle.RegisterMany(services: { Service }): ()`
- `Lifecycle.Start(): ()`
  Run Init() on every queued service (in order), THEN Start() on every service. Idempotent — a second call is a no-op. pcall-isolated so one broken service can't abort the rest.
- `Lifecycle.IsStarted(): boolean`
- `Lifecycle.OnStarted(fn: () -> ()): ()`
  Run `fn` after Start() completes (immediately, on a fresh thread, if already started).

### Types

Exported types (use them in annotations: `local x: Module.TypeName`).

```lua
export type Spec = {
    Name: Types.ServiceName,
    Needs: { {} },
    Init: (() -> ())?,
    Start: (() -> ())?,
    AutoStart: boolean?,
}
export type State = "defined" | "initializing" | "initialized" | "failed"
export type Service = {
    Name: string?,
    Init: ((self: any) -> ())?,
    Start: ((self: any) -> ())?,
    [any]: any,
}
```
